text:
jamie: Heads-up — ap-south1 apiserver started returning 502/504s ~10m ago, controller-manager has restarted 3x. GPU provisioner requests are queuing, backlog ~120. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/infrastructure/d/CP/ap-south1

Rohit: Copy. Looking at apiserver logs now. Any recent NAT/egress changes or infra deploys? :thinking_face:

nina: No infra deploys from ops in the last hour. I saw a spike in watch events and conntrack counts at ~10:02. Could be NAT port exhaustion on cloud-nat.

samira: Ops alert from infra-bot earlier: `cloud-nat-ebs-fallback` toggle tripped 09:58. Might be related.

infra-bot: [alert] cloud-nat-ebs-fallback toggled by autoscale-controller at 2026-03-21T09:58:12Z.

Rohit: Pulling `kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-apiserver-5 --since=15m` now. First glance: a lot of slow request traces and 'too many open connections' warnings.

jamie: Paste of the recent errors from apiserver: ```
E0321 09:59:21.123456 1 controller_manager.go:256] controller failed: Watch closed for resource pods: error reading from connection: read tcp 10.0.2.15:443->10.0.5.200:52924: i/o timeout
E0321 09:59:22.654321 1 apiserver.go:402] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
```

nina: Also seeing conntrack SNAT exhaustion on the NAT metrics: `conntrack_used ~ 97%`, `SNAT_port_free ~ 3%`.

samira: Temporary mitigation idea: move GPU provisioning webhook traffic to controlplane-proxy in a different subnet that uses a secondary NAT pool. That needs a small routing change, I can flip it if we agree.

Rohit: Can we scale apiserver replicas first? If watches are queuing because apiserver is CPU-bound, a scale might buy time while we fix NAT.

jamie: Trying scale now: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment/kube-apiserver --replicas=5`

Rohit: I see new pods coming up. DNS for the internal LB might take a bit.

infra-bot: [deploy] kube-apiserver replicas scaled to 5 by jamie at 2026-03-21T10:01:05Z.

nina: After scale, apiserver CPU dropped from 95% -> 42% across new pods. Request latency improved slightly. But conntrack still high — watch delivery still flaky for long-lived leases.

samira: Flipped GPU-provisioning route to secondary NAT pool. This should reduce SNAT pressure for control plane > worker interactions.

Rohit: Confirming: SNAT_port_free increased to ~18% after reroute. Watch reconnection errors dropping in logs.

jamie: Backlog decreased from ~120 to ~15 in the provisioning queue. Controller-manager restarts stopped. :thumbsup:

samira: We'll keep the route change as a temporary workaround. Action items: 1) schedule a NAT capacity bump in ap-south1 (cloud ticket), 2) add better quota accounting for long-lived watch connections from the GPU provisioner, 3) postmortem on why autoscale-controller toggled fallback.

nina: I'll open the cloud ticket and add dashboard panels for SNAT headroom.

Rohit: I'll follow up on controller-manager logs to ensure no latent memory/GC regression.

jamie: Great. Leaving it in monitoring. If backlog creeps over 50 again, we fallback to Dedicated provisioner.

samira: Noted. I'll also add a short-runbook step for rerouting provisioning traffic to spare NAT pools in emergencies.

jamie: Thanks everyone. Will draft a short incident blurb for the all-hands.

nina: Current status: degraded -> recovering. Will update with ticket #CLOUD-4821 once created.

samira: +1. Good catch on the SNAT.

Rohit: LGTM.

infra-bot: [status] incident resolved -> monitoring.

jamie: Closing thread for now. Follow-up postmortem planned. :white_check_mark:
